{{Short description|Data format for sending a certificate signing request}}
{{use dmy dates|date=October 2021}}
'''SPKAC''' ('''Signed Public Key and Challenge''', also known as '''Netscape SPKI''') is a format for sending a [[certificate signing request]] (CSR): it encodes a [[public key]], that can be manipulated using [[OpenSSL]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.openssl.org/docs/man1.1.0/apps/spkac.html |title=Documents, spkac(1) |publisher=OpenSSL |date= |accessdate=2017-04-05}}</ref> It is created using the little documented [[HTML]] [[keygen]] element<ref>{{cite web|url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/HTML/Element/keygen |title=Html &#124; Mdn |publisher=Developer.mozilla.org |date=2013-08-15 |accessdate=2013-10-13}}</ref> inside a number of [[Netscape (web browser)|Netscape compatible browsers]].

==Standardisation==
There exists an ongoing effort to standardise SPKAC through an [[Internet Draft]] in the [[Internet Engineering Task Force]] (IETF). The purpose of this work has been to formally define what has existed prior as a [[de facto]] standard, and to address security deficiencies, particular with respect to historic insecure use of [[MD5]] that has since been declared unsafe for use with [[Digital signature|digital signatures]].{{Ref RFC|6151}}

==Implementations==
[[HTML5]] originally specified the <code>&lt;keygen&gt;</code> element to support SPKAC in the browser to make it easier to create [[client side]] certificates through a [[web service]] for protocols such as [[WebID]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.w3.org/TR/html5/forms.html#the-keygen-element |title=HTML5 W3C Recommendation 28 October 2014. 4.10.12 The keygen element |publisher=W3C |date=2014-10-28 |accessdate=2016-10-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.w3.org/wiki/WebID |title=WebID: creating a global decentralised authentication protocol |publisher=W3C |accessdate=2013-10-13}}</ref> however, subsequent work for HTML 5.1 placed the keygen element "at-risk", and the first public working draft of HTML 5.2 removes the keygen element entirely.<ref>{{cite mailing list |url=https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-html/2016Jun/0001.html |title=Re: Call for Consensus - Remove &lt;keygen&gt; from HTML |date=2016-06-03 |accessdate=2016-10-17 |mailing-list=W3C HTML Working Group |last=Nevile |first=Chaals }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.w3.org/TR/2016/CR-html51-20160621/#status |title=HTML5.1: CR 21 June 2016. Status of this document |publisher=W3C |date=2016-06-21 |accessdate=2016-10-17}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.w3.org/TR/html52/changes.html#changes-fpwd |title=HTML 5.2: First Public WD. Changes from HTML 5.1 |publisher=W3C |date=2016-08-18 |accessdate=2016-10-17}}</ref> The removal of the keygen element is due to non-interoperability and non-conformity from a standards perspective in addition to security concerns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://w3ctag.github.io/client-certificates |title=Keygen and Client Certificates |publisher=W3C |author=W3C Technical Architecture Group |date=2015-11-30 |accessdate=2016-10-17}}</ref>

The [[World Wide Web Consortium]] (W3C) Web Authentication Working Group developed the [[WebAuthn]] (Web Authentication) API to replace the keygen element.<ref>{{cite mailing list |url=https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/www-tag/2016May/0016.html |title=Re: removing keygen from HTML |date=2016-05-31 |accessdate=2016-10-17 |mailing-list=W3C WWW Technical Architecture Group |last1=Halpin |first1=Harry |last2=Appelquist |first2=Daniel |last3=Mill |first3=Eric |last4=Gmür |first4=Reto }}</ref>

[[Bouncy Castle (cryptography)|Bouncy Castle]] provides a Java class.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bouncycastle.org/docs/docs1.5on/org/bouncycastle/jce/netscape/NetscapeCertRequest.html|title=Bouncy Castle Java Documentation|accessdate=2013-12-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://lists.foaf-project.org/pipermail/foaf-protocols/2009-January/000144.html|title=foaf-protocols&#93; spkac test implementation in Java |publisher=Lists.foaf-project.org |date= |accessdate=2013-10-13}}</ref>

An implementation for [[Erlang (programming language)|Erlang/OTP]] exists too.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://github.com/ztmr/espkac |title=ztmr/espkac @ GitHub |publisher=Github.com |date= |accessdate=2013-10-13}}</ref>

An implementation for [[Python (programming language)|Python]] is named pyspkac.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://github.com/FFM/pyspkac|title=pyspkac|accessdate=2013-12-06|publisher=Github.com}}</ref>

PHP OpenSSL extension as of version 5.6.0.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://php.net/manual/en/migration56.openssl.php|title=php 5.6.0 OpenSSL Native SPKAC support}}</ref>

[[Node.js]] implementation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#crypto_class_certificate|title=node.js spki support}}</ref>

===Deficiencies===
The user interface needs to be improved in browsers, to make it more obvious to users when a server is asking for the [[client certificate]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heise-online.co.uk/security/User-tracking-with-SSL-certificates-in-Firefox--/news/96239 |title=User tracking with SSL certificates in Firefox - The H Security: News and Features |publisher=Heise-online.co.uk |date=2007-09-19 |accessdate=2013-10-13 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080919045733/http://www.heise-online.co.uk/security/User-tracking-with-SSL-certificates-in-Firefox--/news/96239 |archivedate=2008-09-19 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
